_note: Điểm đến trong bán kính một ngày đi về, tính từ tâm mỗi vùng. KHÔNG PHẢI DỮ LIỆU GIÁ và không phải xếp hạng của Nón Lá — app chưa quét menu ở những nơi này. `at` là toạ độ điểm đến, khoảng cách hiện trên giao diện được TÍNH từ toạ độ đó chứ không ghi trong tệp này; `travel` là cách đi và thời gian đi điển hình, do người viết ghi lại, nên nó là ước lượng chứ không phải kết quả đo. `ticket` là giá vé niêm yết tại thời điểm ghi — vé tham quan ở Việt Nam đổi theo năm, hãy coi nó là bậc giá chứ không phải con số để mặc cả. `zone` trỏ sang một vùng mà app có sẵn bản đồ và dữ liệu giá.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 45–60 min by taxi, or the yellow bus from Hội An bus station
hoian-oldtown.blurb: The nearest big city: a river cut through the middle of it, six bridges, and a food scene that owes nothing to tourists.
hoian-oldtown.tip: The dragon bridge breathes fire and water at 21:00 on Saturday and Sunday. Stand on the east bank, upwind.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 50–65 min by taxi from the old town
hoian-oldtown.blurb: Thirty kilometres of open sand on the east side of Đà Nẵng, with a seafood strip behind it.
hoian-oldtown.tip: Seafood on the beach road is charged by weight. Ask the price per kilo and watch the scale before it goes to the kitchen.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 25–35 min by taxi, halfway to Đà Nẵng
hoian-oldtown.blurb: Five limestone outcrops full of caves, with Buddhist shrines cut into the rock and a view over the coast from the top.
hoian-oldtown.tip: Go early. The caves are cool, the stairs between them are not, and the marble carving village at the base sells by weight.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 60–75 min by taxi or tour bus, inland
hoian-oldtown.ticket: 150.000₫ including the shuttle and dance show
hoian-oldtown.blurb: Brick towers the Cham built between the 4th and 13th centuries, half-swallowed by jungle and half-flattened by 1969 bombing.
hoian-oldtown.tip: First bus at 05:00 gets you there before the heat and before the crowds. Nothing is shaded.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 25 min by speedboat from Cửa Đại pier
hoian-oldtown.ticket: 70.000₫ marine park fee, plus the boat
hoian-oldtown.blurb: A cluster of islands an hour off the coast, with clear water, one main village and a hard ban on plastic bags.
hoian-oldtown.tip: Boats stop when the sea gets up, usually October to February. Book the day before and check the morning forecast.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 75–90 min by taxi, then the cable car up
hoian-oldtown.ticket: around 900.000₫ for the cable car and park
hoian-oldtown.blurb: A French hill station turned theme park at 1,400 m, reached by one of the longest cable cars in the world. The golden hands bridge is here.
hoian-oldtown.tip: It is a theme park, not a mountain village — go for the ride up and the temperature drop, and expect queues.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 15 min by bicycle or taxi east of the old town
hoian-oldtown.blurb: Water coconut palms in the brackish river, worked from round bamboo basket boats.
hoian-oldtown.tip: The loud boat-spinning shows come with a tip expectation. Say no at the start if you want the quiet version.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 15 min by bicycle from the old town
hoian-oldtown.blurb: The closest beach to Hội An, with a line of low-key bars on the sand.
hoian-oldtown.tip: Sun loungers are usually free if you order a drink. Check before you sit down, not after.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 10 min by bicycle west along the river
hoian-oldtown.blurb: A working pottery village on the river bank, throwing on foot-turned wheels the way it has for five centuries.
hoian-oldtown.tip: The terracotta park at the far end is a separate, more expensive ticket. The village itself is the interesting half.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 12 min by bicycle north of the old town
hoian-oldtown.blurb: The market garden that supplies the old town's herbs, fertilised with lake weed instead of chemicals.
hoian-oldtown.tip: Half the herbs on your cao lầu came from these beds. Cooking classes here are cheaper booked at the village than through a hotel.

hoian-oldtown.travel: 2 h by car, usually on the way to Huế
hoian-oldtown.blurb: The pass over the spur of mountain that splits Vietnam's weather in two. Old French and American bunkers at the top.
hoian-oldtown.tip: Cloud sits on the pass most afternoons. Cross in the morning if you want the view you came for.

danang-hanriver.travel: 45–60 min by taxi, or the yellow bus from Đà Nẵng bus station
danang-hanriver.ticket: 120.000₫ for the old-town ticket, five sights
danang-hanriver.blurb: A merchant port that stopped growing in the 19th century and never got rebuilt. Lanterns, tailors and the best cao lầu in the country.
danang-hanriver.tip: The town charges an entry ticket to the protected core. Buy it at a booth, not from someone who approaches you on the street.

danang-hanriver.travel: 10 min by taxi across the Rồng or Trần Thị Lý bridge
danang-hanriver.blurb: The city's own beach, wide and open, five minutes from the centre.
danang-hanriver.tip: Seafood on the beach road runs 25–40% above the same dish in town. That is the view charge, and it is worth knowing before you sit down.

danang-hanriver.n: Bán đảo Sơn Trà · Chùa Linh Ứng
danang-hanriver.en: Son Tra Peninsula · Linh Ung Pagoda
danang-hanriver.travel: 25 min by taxi north along the coast road
danang-hanriver.blurb: A forested headland with a 67 m white Guanyin statue looking out to sea, and red-shanked douc langurs in the trees above the road.
danang-hanriver.tip: Motorbike rental shops will rent you a bike for the loop; several of the upper roads are steep enough that they should not. Take a car.

danang-hanriver.travel: 20 min by taxi south along the coast
danang-hanriver.blurb: Five limestone outcrops full of caves, with Buddhist shrines cut into the rock and a view over the coast from the top.
danang-hanriver.tip: The marble carving shops at the base sell by weight and ship home. Get the shipping quote before you agree the stone price.

danang-hanriver.travel: 45–60 min by taxi, then the cable car up
danang-hanriver.ticket: around 900.000₫ for the cable car and park
danang-hanriver.blurb: A French hill station turned theme park at 1,400 m, reached by one of the longest cable cars in the world. The golden hands bridge is here.
danang-hanriver.tip: Go on a weekday and get the first cable car. By 11:00 the bridge is a queue with a view.

danang-hanriver.blurb: The pass over the spur of mountain that splits Vietnam's weather in two. Old French and American bunkers at the top.
danang-hanriver.tip: Trucks take the tunnel, so the old road is quiet. Cloud sits on it most afternoons — go in the morning.

danang-hanriver.travel: 2.5 h by car over Hải Vân, or 3 h by train along the coast
danang-hanriver.blurb: The imperial capital until 1945: a walled citadel, a river, and the most particular food in Vietnam.
danang-hanriver.tip: The coastal train from Đà Nẵng is one of the best rail rides in Asia and costs a fraction of a private car. Sit on the left going north.

danang-hanriver.n: Suối khoáng nóng Núi Thần Tài
danang-hanriver.travel: 45 min by taxi west into the hills
danang-hanriver.blurb: Hot mineral pools in forest at the foot of the Bà Nà range, with a water park attached.
danang-hanriver.tip: Pair it with Bà Nà only if you have a full day and a driver waiting — public transport out here is thin.

danang-mykhe.travel: 10 min by taxi west across the river
danang-mykhe.blurb: The other side of the bridges: markets, the Cham museum, and the same dishes for noticeably less than on the beach road.
danang-mykhe.tip: Chợ Cồn and Chợ Hàn are where the city actually eats. Both close their food sections by early evening.

danang-mykhe.n: Bán đảo Sơn Trà · Chùa Linh Ứng
danang-mykhe.en: Son Tra Peninsula · Linh Ung Pagoda
danang-mykhe.travel: 15 min by taxi north along the beach road
danang-mykhe.blurb: A forested headland with a 67 m white Guanyin statue looking out to sea, and rare langurs in the trees above the road.
danang-mykhe.tip: Sunrise from the beach here, then the pagoda before the tour buses arrive at nine.

danang-mykhe.travel: 15 min by taxi south along the beach road
danang-mykhe.blurb: Five limestone outcrops full of caves, with shrines cut into the rock and a view back over the whole beach.
danang-mykhe.tip: The lift saves the first climb only. Everything after that is stairs — bring water, not flip-flops.

danang-mykhe.travel: 40–50 min by taxi down the coast road
danang-mykhe.ticket: 120.000₫ for the old-town ticket, five sights
danang-mykhe.blurb: A merchant port that stopped growing in the 19th century and never got rebuilt. Lanterns, tailors and the best cao lầu in the country.
danang-mykhe.tip: The coast road passes An Bàng beach — a decent half-day stop on the way back.

danang-mykhe.travel: 30 min by taxi south along the coast
danang-mykhe.blurb: Quieter sand than Mỹ Khê with a line of low-key bars, halfway to Hội An.
danang-mykhe.tip: Fewer high-rises, more shade, and the seafood is priced closer to town rates.

danang-mykhe.travel: 50 min to Cửa Đại pier, then 25 min by speedboat
danang-mykhe.ticket: 70.000₫ marine park fee, plus the boat
danang-mykhe.blurb: Islands an hour off the coast with clear water, one main village and a hard ban on plastic bags.
danang-mykhe.tip: Sea state closes the crossing from roughly October to February. Check the morning before you commit to a boat.

hue-citadel.travel: 15 min by taxi, or 40 min by dragon boat upriver
hue-citadel.blurb: A seven-storey brick tower over the Perfume River, and the Austin car that carried Thích Quảng Đức to Saigon in 1963.
hue-citadel.tip: The dragon boats sell a river trip that stops here; agree the full price and the return time before boarding.

hue-citadel.blurb: A concrete-and-mosaic hillside tomb that looks like nothing else in Vietnam — French gothic outside, glass and porcelain inside.
hue-citadel.tip: The most decorated of the tombs and the smallest. Half an hour is enough.

hue-citadel.blurb: Less a tomb than a walled garden retreat with a lake, built while the emperor was alive so he could use it.
hue-citadel.tip: The largest of the three main tombs, and the one worth the most walking time.

hue-citadel.travel: 30 min by taxi south, past the river fork
hue-citadel.blurb: The most symmetrical of the imperial tombs: one long axis of gates, courtyards and lakes running through pine forest.
hue-citadel.tip: A combined ticket covering the citadel and three tombs costs less than buying them separately. Ask for it at the first gate.

hue-citadel.travel: 70 min by car south, at the foot of Hải Vân
hue-citadel.blurb: A sand bar between a lagoon and the sea, usually seen from the train window on the way to Đà Nẵng.
hue-citadel.tip: The lagoon side has the oyster and mussel places; the sea side has the hotels.

hue-citadel.travel: 90 min by car south-west, then a park vehicle up
hue-citadel.ticket: 60.000₫ entry, plus the shuttle up the mountain
hue-citadel.blurb: Cloud forest rising to 1,450 m, with a five-tier waterfall and the ruins of a French hill station near the summit.
hue-citadel.tip: Rain is the default here even when Huế is dry. It is a full day, and the last shuttle down leaves earlier than you expect.

hue-citadel.blurb: The largest lagoon in South-East Asia, worked with fish traps and flat-bottomed boats. Best at sunset.
hue-citadel.tip: Sunset boat trips are arranged in the villages on the shore, not in Huế. Fix the price and the hours before you push off.

hue-citadel.travel: 2.5 h by car over Hải Vân, or 3 h by train along the coast
hue-citadel.blurb: The nearest big city, on the far side of the pass: bridges, beaches and cheaper food than the tourist end of Huế.
hue-citadel.tip: Take the train at least one way. It runs along the cliff between the pass and the sea, and the ticket costs less than a taxi's petrol.

hue-citadel.travel: 3–3.5 h by car south, usually with a stop at Hải Vân
hue-citadel.ticket: 120.000₫ for the old-town ticket, five sights
hue-citadel.blurb: A merchant port that stopped growing in the 19th century and never got rebuilt. The other end of the central Vietnam run.
hue-citadel.tip: Most people do this as a one-way transfer with stops, not a day trip. Ask for the Hải Vân route, not the tunnel.

hanoi-hoankiem.travel: 2 h by car, or 2.5 h by train to Ninh Bình
hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: Limestone karst standing in flooded rice fields, rowed through by women using their feet on the oars. Halong Bay without the sea.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: Three boat routes; the longest passes the most caves. Tip the rower at the end — it is expected and they are paid almost nothing per trip.

hanoi-hoankiem.travel: 2.5 h by expressway coach from Hà Nội
hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: Two thousand limestone islands in a shallow green sea. The reason most people come to northern Vietnam.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: A day trip is six hours of bus for four hours of boat. One overnight on the water is the version worth doing.

hanoi-hoankiem.travel: 2 h by car south-west, then a rowed boat up the stream
hanoi-hoankiem.ticket: 80.000₫ entry and boat, plus the cable car
hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: A complex of temples in a river valley, ending in a cave shrine reached by boat and then a climb.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: The pilgrimage festival runs from the second lunar month for six weeks — spectacular, and impossibly crowded.

hanoi-hoankiem.travel: 30 min by taxi, or bus 47A from Long Biên
hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: A seven-century-old ceramics village across the Red River, still firing for the whole country.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: Cheapest half-day out of Hà Nội. Prices in the covered market are a third of the same piece in the old quarter.

hanoi-hoankiem.travel: 10 min by taxi west of the lake
hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: A thousand years of capital, layered on one site: Lý foundations, a Nguyễn gate, and the concrete bunker where the 1972 air war was run.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: The bunker (D67) is the part most people miss. It is behind the main hall and included in the same ticket.

hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: The clearest explanation anywhere of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups, with full-size houses rebuilt in the garden behind.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: The outdoor section is the good half and takes an hour on its own. Go on a dry day.

hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: A laterite-brick farming village that kept its 17th-century layout, gates and communal house.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: People still live and farm here. It is not an open-air museum — ask before walking into a courtyard.

hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: A French hill station at 900 m, ten degrees cooler than the delta and usually inside a cloud.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: The view is a lottery. If Hà Nội is clear and dry, the odds are better.

hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: A flat green valley of rice and White Thai stilt houses, ringed by limestone.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: Worth an overnight rather than a day trip. The homestays in Lác and Pom Coọng are the whole point.

hanoi-hoankiem.travel: 5–6 h by expressway coach, or the night train to Lào Cai
hanoi-hoankiem.blurb: Terraced rice mountains on the Chinese border, and the Hmong and Dao villages that farm them.
hanoi-hoankiem.tip: Not a day trip — two nights minimum. Book a village guide directly rather than a bus tour if you want to walk rather than shop.

hcmc-district1.travel: 90 min by car north-west, or 2 h by speedboat up the Saigon River
hcmc-district1.ticket: 125.000₫ at Bến Dược, 90.000₫ at Bến Đình
hcmc-district1.blurb: Two hundred kilometres of hand-dug tunnel used through the war, part of it widened so visitors can crawl through a stretch.
hcmc-district1.tip: Bến Dược is further out, less rebuilt and much less crowded than Bến Đình. The firing range is optional and loud.

hcmc-district1.blurb: The closest slice of the Mekong: river islands, coconut candy workshops and sampans down the palm channels.
hcmc-district1.tip: The standard tour is heavily packaged. Cần Thơ is three more hours and a different, better delta.

hcmc-district1.travel: 2 h by car, or 90 min by hydrofoil down the river
hcmc-district1.blurb: The city's weekend beach on a headland, with a Christ statue you can climb the inside of.
hcmc-district1.tip: Saturday traffic on the coast road is punishing. The hydrofoil costs more and takes half as long.

hcmc-district1.travel: 90 min by car south-east, across the Bình Khánh ferry
hcmc-district1.blurb: A UNESCO biosphere of replanted mangrove — defoliated in the war, put back by hand from the 1970s.
hcmc-district1.tip: The monkey island section is a tourist stop with aggressive macaques. Keep bags shut and phones away.

hcmc-district1.travel: 2.5 h by car north-west, usually combined with Củ Chi
hcmc-district1.blurb: A single 986 m cone rising out of flat delta, with a cable car to the summit and the Cao Đài Holy See on the way.
hcmc-district1.tip: The Cao Đài midday ceremony at noon is the reason to time the trip. Visitors watch from the balcony, shoes off.

hcmc-district1.n: Cần Thơ · Chợ nổi Cái Răng
hcmc-district1.en: Can Tho · Cai Rang Floating Market
hcmc-district1.travel: 3.5 h by car or coach south-west
hcmc-district1.blurb: The delta's biggest wholesale market, done boat to boat at dawn, with each trader's goods hung from a pole.
hcmc-district1.tip: It is a wholesale market that empties by eight. On the water before six or not at all — which means staying the night.

hcmc-district1.n: Bán đảo Thanh Đa · Bình Quới
hcmc-district1.blurb: A loop of the Saigon River still in the city, with garden restaurants and a rural feel ten minutes from a motorway.
hcmc-district1.tip: The weekend buffet places here are the closest thing to delta food without leaving town.
